I've passed this to the team so they can confirm the details with you directly, and they will follow up shortly.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: RMA APPROVED by Georges for NerdOctaxe on Shop···· (Approved: warranty RMA for the NerdOctaxe 12TH/s on Shop···· (the new PSU did not fix it, so it is the miner). Open the return and send him the prepaid label. The NerdOctaxe is out of stock, so offer him a Hammer Thor P2 (in stock, ships from our US warehouse) as the warranty replacement at no ex). Hal's verdict: defective (Board-level short / dead board: unit will not power on with a known-good replacement PSU, supply goes straight into protection (squeak, single fan twitch, no screen, no lights, no hashing).). Do the rest now, in this order: 1) order-swap skill: return_order.py plan, then create --confirmed (the return reference is the order number plus RMA, the label link comes back); 2) tell the customer: the return is approved, here is the prepaid label, write the reference on the box, and what replacement we can send; 3) ONLY once they agree to that replacement in their own words, rma_replacement.py create --customer-chose "<their words, date>" for the same order (a $0 order held on both sides until the unit is back with us; it releases by itself when the warehouse receives it). Never create it before their yes: an offer is a message, not an order (Nov 11 2026). The tool re-checks stock then: if the unit is now only a pre-order it refuses and names the date; tell them and re-run with --preorder-agreed only on their yes to that date. If any step stops, flag it and tell them the team will confirm the next step by email.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
